A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPR research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebQSP and CWQ experiments, component ablations, and a TreeG search-budget study.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and reports additional PQ/PQL evaluations, expanded-graph experiments, and PUCT rollout and LLM-hint sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: Section 4.1.1 changes the specified negative-path construction from deviations at the last hop to deviations at every hop, using relation/entity-pair mismatches. This modifies training-example construction within the retained CPR framework; RCVNet, its ranking loss, TreeG, and query-level calibration remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from WebQSP and CWQ query-specific subgraphs to PQ and PQL evaluated over their supplied KGs. Section 5.5 also adds an expanded-WebQSP scenario using unified graphs assembled across each split, including a test graph with 778,692 nodes.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparisons retain UaG, CLM, LoFreeCP, and the existing CPR ablations; PQ/PQL reuse this set. The additional studies reuse UaG and the no-PUCT/random-sampling control, whose zero-rollout results match the existing ablation's 52.5% ECR and 3.02 APSS at alpha = 0.7.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include split-level graph aggregation, a WebQSP rollout-budget sweep from random sampling through 64 rollouts at alpha = 0.7, and Qwen3-8B/4B/1.7B/0.6B/no-hint comparisons at alpha = 0.8. The original benchmark splits, metrics, risk-level sweep, and default training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of graph-scale robustness, sensitivity to PUCT rollout budgets, and dependence on LLM hint quality, including complete hint removal. Component ablations also extend to PQ/PQL. The original TreeG search-budget analysis is retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates. PUCT rollout counts describe search budgets, not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: All 12 original WebQSP/CWQ result rows in Table 2 are unchanged. Substantial new results appear for PQ/PQL and the added analyses: expanded-WebQSP CPR achieves 55.3% ECR with 10.10 APSS at alpha = 0.5, while no-hint CPR achieves 42.0% ECR with 2.54 APSS at alpha = 0.8. These are additional settings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The formal negative-path set definition in Section 4.1.1 changes from terminal-entity deviations to a union of relation/entity deviations across all hops. Theorem 4.1, its exchangeability assumptions, and the six-step Appendix A proof remain substantively unchanged; other mathematical edits mainly align scoring notation.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the claimed ECR improvement from 34% to 45% and prediction-set-size reduction from 40% to 52%, alongside broader benchmark coverage. The central contributions—query-level calibration of path scores and PUCT-trained RCVNet—remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations about scalability, rollout-budget trade-offs, and reliability under degraded or absent LLM hints. Appendix E attributes CPR's robustness to soft hint-based scoring and contrasts this with UaG's claimed hard dependence on LLM outputs. Section 4.1.1 also explains how intermediate-hop negatives discourage optimistic scores for early-diverging paths.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-availability link, specifies PQ/PQL maximum hop depths, and explains positive-path generation in the no-PUCT ablation. Figure 3 additionally documents conditioner dimensions and tanh processing. Hardware, embeddings, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and training epochs remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guo et al. (2025), Guo et al. (2026), and Zhou et al. (2018), while retaining its principal positioning against existing KGQA and conformal methods. Several other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the methodology undergo extensive rephrasing, with revised contribution wording and additional internal headings. The experimental narrative is reorganized around scalability and efficiency/sensitivity, implementation information is consolidated in Appendix C, and appendices D/E and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 expand to four datasets, and Tables 3–6 add graph statistics and supplementary comparisons. Figure 3 is substantially redrawn to separate conditioning and scalar-feature processing and show FiLM connections. Figure 1 gains panel labels and a revised caption; Figure 2 is restyled and relocated with its results retained.

improvement.justification: The added graph-scale, rollout, and LLM-hint studies address empirical questions left open in v1, while clearer architecture documentation and a code pointer improve reproducibility information. Reporting errors limit the gain: Table 2's new PQL efficiency of 6.57% at alpha = 0.3 conflicts with 71.3/20.85, approximately 3.42%. Section 5.5 also claims expanded-graph CPR exceeds original-graph UaG at every risk level, although Table 4 gives 12.3% versus 15.3% at alpha = 0.8. These weaken the stronger conclusions without eliminating the added empirical value.
